column1: # boru Language Specification: forward-collection edge cases I —
# greediness, the ONE split rule, barriers, type-directed stopping.
# modifiers.tsv (the /… suffix matrix). These rows pin the COLLECTION

# a call are the same ONE split (eng/go/CLAUDE.md §Signature Ordering:
# forward args fill sig positions 0..k-1 in written order, the rest
# fill backward from the stack prefix), and where collection stops —
# `end`, `;`, `)`, an empty `()`, another function word, or a type
# NOTE: a newline is NOT a barrier (EXPLANATION.md §stack) — the TSV
# format cannot hold multi-line inputs, so the newline rows live here
# as their single-line equivalents: every multi-statement row below is
# exactly what the same tokens split across lines would evaluate to.

column1: # §2b  three arguments, one rule: for sig order (a, b, c) all of
#      f a b c ≡ c f a b ≡ c b f a ≡ c b a f are the same call, and
#      every OTHER mixed split is a different assignment. The probe fn
#      encodes the assignment in decimal digits: a*100 + b*10 + c.
def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] f3 1 2 3
column3: all-forward: a=1 b=2 c=3

column1: # §3c  the statement boundary does NOT protect a stack value from the
#      NEXT word's optional bigger arity: range has a 3-arg overload,
#      so a lone prior result is claimed as its step argument. Pinned
#      loudly — the protections are arity pinning (/2), grouping, or

column3: range's optional step slot claims the stacked 99: range(2, 4, step 99)
`;` only stops FORWARD collection — the stack claim still happens
end is no protection either
/2 pins the two-arg overload: the 99 survives
filling the optional slot explicitly also protects
a paren GROUP is a real scope: the inner range cannot see the 99
type pruning protects: slice's 3-arg form needs an Integer where the list sits
